steps.title: See today's market at a glance
steps.narration: The homepage opens straight to today's market score. There's no setup and nothing to wait for.
steps.point_out: The Market Regime score, already filled in on the very first load.

steps.title: Browse the ranked stock list
steps.narration: The Stocks page lists ranked companies right away. Familiar names, like Travelers, show up immediately.
steps.point_out: A ranked list of stocks, filled in already.

steps.title: Open one stock's own page
steps.narration: Clicking into one stock, like Apple, shows its price and history at once. No extra lookup step is needed.
steps.point_out: Apple's price and history, right there on the page.

steps.title: Check how stocks group by sector
steps.narration: Sectors group related companies and funds together. This one groups cybersecurity names, including the fund HACK.
steps.point_out: Real sector groupings, not placeholders.

steps.title: See the record behind every claim
steps.narration: The Evidence page keeps a running ledger of certified claims. A pattern only counts as proven once it earns a place on this ledger.
steps.point_out: The certified-claims ledger.

steps.title: Check a personal watchlist
steps.narration: A personal watchlist works too. This one includes Johnson & Johnson, with real figures attached.
steps.point_out: Real holdings on the watchlist, not sample data.

steps.title: Try the event-study research tool
steps.narration: A dedicated research tool lets you set up and study patterns around chosen events.
steps.point_out: The event-study setup panel.

steps.title: Open Data Manager while it's still starting up
steps.narration: The Data Manager page shows its run history right away. The app never makes you wait for it to finish starting up first.
steps.point_out: The run history list, ready immediately.

steps.title: See when work is happening in the background
steps.narration: If the app is still crunching numbers behind the scenes, it says so plainly on this page. Nothing is hidden.
steps.point_out: The background-compute status.

steps.title: Pick a date range to check
steps.narration: Typing in a start date begins a new data check.
steps.point_out: The start-date field being filled in.

steps.title: Set the end of the range
steps.narration: A two-day range is entered, covering a weekend with no trading days.
steps.point_out: The end-date field being filled in.

steps.title: Submit the request
steps.narration: One click submits the request. No extra confirmation step is needed for a plain check like this.
steps.point_out: The Start button being pressed.

steps.title: An honest answer when there's nothing new to do
steps.narration: Weekends have no trading days, so the app says plainly that no new snapshots were needed. It never pretends to have done work it didn't do.
steps.point_out: The message explaining why nothing new was created.

steps.title: Ask for a much longer stretch of history
steps.narration: This time the start date reaches back over a year.
steps.point_out: The start-date field.

steps.title: Set a far-out end date
steps.narration: The end date is set more than a year after the start. That's a much bigger request than a single day.
steps.point_out: The end-date field.

steps.title: Submit the long-range request
steps.narration: One click submits the whole multi-year request at once.
steps.point_out: The Start button being pressed again.

steps.title: No artificial limit on how much you can request
steps.narration: The app accepts the whole range in one request. That's 412 calendar days, with no need to split it into smaller chunks.
steps.point_out: The accepted range, covering all 412 calendar days.

steps.title: Look up a past scan instantly
steps.narration: Opening a specific day from years ago, like February 15, 2018, is instant. It was already worked out when the data first came in, so nothing needs recomputing now.
steps.point_out: A stored snapshot from that exact day, served instantly.

steps.title: Open the time-machine view of the market
steps.narration: The Backtest page loads cleanly on its own. It never has to wait on heavier work that might be running elsewhere.
steps.point_out: The time-machine control at the top of the page.

steps.title: Revisit a specific day without recomputing it
steps.narration: Looking up March 15, 2018 again shows the exact same numbers right away. The app reads what it already saved instead of redoing the work.
steps.point_out: The historical badge and scorecard for that exact date.
